domain_model: form_binding(tenant_id, process_key, form_key, fields, layout, version). process_key = real published process definition key (validated indirectly by classifyLayoutSave's live-schema resolution via process_app_binding -> registry_def, fail-closed 409 WRONG_FLOOR if unresolvable). form_key === stepKey in the actor-scoped API = the BPMN userTask id, matching inbox item.step. fields: BindingField[] = the per-step LIVE schema snapshot (key/type/required/label/contract/presentation/options/mode) — mode (T-0404) is the SERVER-SIDE per-step policy (read-only/required-to-advance/hidden), independent of layout. layout: FormDocument|null = the declarative tree (form-document.js {schemaVersion,source,root,step?}) assembled by a human (FormDesigner) or an agent (T-0656 document-ops seam) — null for legacy bindings saved before T-0506/without a layout.
layout_flow: FormDesigner: process+step picker (NEW, F1) -> GET /api/forms/binding?processKey&stepKey (NEW read, F3) -> if layout present+valid(.root): initHistory(layout) instead of buildDefaultDocument, else unchanged schema-driven build -> user edits via existing form-document-ops -> Save button writes doc.step from the picker (NEW, F2) -> POST /api/forms/binding {process_key, form_key, layout} (route unchanged, already accepted layout since T-0656) -> classifyLayoutSave gate (unchanged) -> persisted to form_binding.layout (column existed, T-0506). Agent path (T-0656 document-ops) is untouched and writes the same column. Consumption: GET /api/forms/binding now ALSO returns layout when non-null (NEW, F4, both the T-0072 named route and the T-0376 actor-scoped route used by InboxTaskForm) -> InboxTaskForm (screen-inbox.jsx) branches on binding.layout having a valid .root -> renders via the SAME FormDocumentRenderer FormDesigner already uses as its live preview (NEW consumer, F5), with binding.fields (the LIVE per-step schema) as the type/mode/options source -> a legacy binding (no layout key in the GET response at all) renders via the untouched per-row FieldControl path (NF3).
ui_built: FormDesigner.jsx gained a 'Привязка' section above the existing Приложение/Набор полей picker: (1) a process <Select> populated from /api/process-catalog filtered to status==='published' (real tenant data, D-064 anti-case — no hardcoded slug list), with loading/error/empty states matching FormBuilder.jsx's existing pattern; (2) a free-text 'Шаг процесса' input (same convention as FormBuilder.jsx's existing step field) with an HTML <datalist> populated by best-effort userTask id/name suggestions parsed from the chosen process's real bpmnXml via the new pure module web/src/forms/bpmn-user-tasks.js (extractUserTasks — a regex-based scanner, not a DOMParser/bpmn-moddle integration, so it works identically in the jsdom-less vitest 'node' tier and the browser); (3) selecting process+step triggers a GET /api/forms/binding lookup — an existing layout short-circuits the schema-driven document rebuild (a ref-guarded skip so the registry-def-change effect does not immediately clobber the just-loaded layout); (4) the Save button is disabled with a visible Russian hint ('Выберите процесс и шаг выше, чтобы сохранить форму.') until a process+step is chosen OR the document already carries doc.step (e.g. an AI-emitted/embedded document) — this is what directly closes the P0 (persistLayout can no longer silently fall through to the dead 'record'/'record-form' pair when a real binding was intended).
renderer_application: InboxTaskForm (web/src/screens/screen-inbox.jsx) computes `hasLayout = binding.layout && typeof binding.layout === 'object' && binding.layout.root` and branches: true -> <FormDocumentRenderer document={binding.layout} fields={fieldsWithRecordId} values={values} onChange={handleChange} errors={fieldErrors} /> (the SAME renderer FormDesigner uses as its live preview — one tree-walker, not a second copy); false -> the original per-row FieldControl.map(...) loop, byte-identical to before. Submit-time validation (resolveFieldMode/editableKeys in handleSubmit) is UNCHANGED and reads binding.fields regardless of render path, so required/hidden/read-only enforcement on submit is identical for both paths. A companion fix landed in FormDocumentRenderer.jsx's renderableField(): mode now prioritizes schemaField.mode (the server per-step policy, form_binding.fields[].mode) over the layout node's own authoring-time node.mode — without this, a field the process author marked hidden/read-only/required AT THIS STEP would have rendered wrong (editable/visible) specifically under the new layout path while the legacy path enforced it correctly on the SAME binding; recordId also now passes through the same field so FileField keeps its record context under the layout path.
backward_compat: A form_binding row saved before layout existed (or saved via the plain fields-only body) has layout=NULL in Postgres. src/http/binding.ts omits the `layout` key from the JSON response entirely when NULL (never sends `layout:null` or `layout:{}`) — so a client can branch on `'layout' in data`, which is exactly what InboxTaskForm's `hasLayout` check does (it further requires a valid `.root`, defending against a malformed/partial layout too). This means: legacy bindings continue to save (POST body without `layout` still works, unchanged validation), continue to be read (GET response shape for them is IDENTICAL to before this task), and continue to render (InboxTaskForm's else-branch is the untouched original FieldControl.map loop). All pre-existing screen-inbox.test.jsx assertions pass unmodified — no existing expectation was edited to accommodate this feature.

live_proof.p0_found: InboxTaskForm (web/src/screens/screen-inbox.jsx line ~189) does `const fields = binding.fields || []; if (fields.length === 0) return null;` BEFORE computing `hasLayout` (line ~210). src/http/binding.ts's POST handler (line ~543-545) stores `fields = []` whenever the request carries `layout` but no explicit `fields` key — which is exactly what FormDesigner.jsx's persistLayout() always sends (confirmed live: GET after save returned `"fields":[]` in the body). Net effect: ANY form assembled via the flagship FormDesigner drag-n-drop path renders as 'no form' (early return null) for the assignee — the F5 layout-render branch is unreachable in practice. screen-inbox.test.jsx's T-0665-F5 tests are source-presence only (assert the branch text exists) and do not catch the guard-ordering bug.
medium_findings: FormDesigner's application picker is independent of process_app_binding — an operator can pick any process + any unrelated application; authoring shows no error, only Save's 409 (no registry binding) reveals the mismatch.

telLinear (the reference ТЭЛ process, source=engine/status=deployed, 25 live instances, the one process with a battle-tested live-schema resolution) is excluded from the process picker by the status==='published' filter (modeler-only processes pass).

A field with type==='money' (not number+widget) breaks default form assembly: widget-registry.js's WIDGET_COMPAT_TABLE has no 'money' key, so nodeTypeForFieldType defaults to 'field'/contract scalar, which resolveFieldContract({type:'money'}) never satisfies — V-CONTRACT authoring error on any money field included by default build.

The step datalist suggestion's <option value> is the BPMN userTask id (e.g. Activity_0dsh0ls), not its human-readable name — but the real inbox item.step used by InboxTaskForm's GET query is the human-readable name (e.g. 'Согласование'). Picking the suggested id silently creates a binding that will never resolve for any real inbox task (no error at save time).

findings: FormDocumentRenderer.jsx's renderableField() had a latent mode-source bug independent of this task's 3 assigned gaps: it derived per-step field mode ONLY from the layout node's own node.mode, never from the schema field's server-side per-step mode (form_binding.fields[].mode, T-0404) that the legacy FieldControl-per-row path already enforces. Fixed in-scope (F6) because leaving it would have made the NEW layout render path behave differently from the legacy path on the exact same binding data (a field marked hidden/read-only at this step would have rendered wrong only under the new path) — a regression this task would have introduced if left alone, not merely a pre-existing gap.

The BPMN userTask suggestion list (bpmn-user-tasks.js) is best-effort regex parsing, not a full bpmn-moddle integration — sufficient for a suggestion affordance (the step field remains free text either way) but would not catch every conceivable BPMN 2.0 XML edge case (e.g. CDATA-wrapped attributes, which are not legal XML attribute syntax anyway). Acceptable per ADR §3.1/out_of_scope.
deviations_from_adr: ADR §3.4 anticipated only a mode-priority fix in renderableField; while implementing it, recordId passthrough was also added to the same function (not originally called out in the ADR's F5 description) because omitting it would have silently broken FileField's record-context specifically under the new layout render path — an omission-by-silence regression the ADR's own NF3 backward-compat principle argues against. Documented here rather than in a separate ADR revision since it is a strict extension of the same merge (schemaField properties flowing through), not a new decision.

renderToStaticMarkup (the web test tier's only rendering mechanism — no jsdom/@testing-library) never fires useEffect, so any component whose network-dependent state lives behind an effect (FormDesigner's applications/processCatalog, InboxTaskForm's binding) cannot be exercised end-to-end in a synchronous static-markup render. Resolved per-file: FormDesigner's picker UI is verified via source-presence assertions (matching the file's own established pattern for the T-0656 fullscreen invariant) plus one static-markup test of the save-gate that IS reachable synchronously via the initialDocument/initialFields embedding shortcut; InboxTaskForm/screen-inbox follows the file's pre-existing 100%-source-presence convention (already true before this task, e.g. the T-0579/T-0608 tests); FormDocumentRenderer/FormNode ARE plain functions with no hooks in their own body, so those got real tree-walk behavioral tests (mirroring FormDocumentRenderer.test.jsx's and field-renderer-file.test.jsx's pre-existing approach of calling the function directly and inspecting the returned element tree).
